question: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 15%, then find the percentage increase in its volume. (Rounded up to 2 decimal places.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume ∝ r³

Increase factor = (1 + 0.15)³ = (1.15)³

= 1.520875

% increase = (1.520875 − 1) × 100

**∴ Answer = 52.09%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in radius = 15%

**Formula used:**

Volume of sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let original radius = r

⇒ New radius = 1.15r

⇒ Original volume = (4/3)πr³

⇒ New volume = (4/3)π(1.15r)³

⇒ = (4/3)π × 1.15³ × r³

⇒ Ratio of volumes = 1.15³

⇒ = 1.520875

⇒ Increase = (1.520875 − 1) × 100

⇒ = 52.0875%

⇒ ≈ 52.09%

**∴ The correct answer is 52.09%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Power Rule

If quantity ∝ rⁿ, then % change ≈ n × % change (approximation).

Exact Formula

New value = Old × (1 + x/100)ⁿ

Sphere Volume

Volume = (4/3)πr³
